reader.requirement: At --std 85, with two or more delimiters the examination must stop at the first position where any delimiter matches, testing the delimiters at that position in the order written so the first listed match wins, treat the matched characters as one delimiter, and never let a character serve in two delimiters (the scan resumes after the matched occurrence, an ALL phrase consuming only repeats of the delimiter it matched).

reader.notes: UnstringExtract takes the earliest position over all delimiters with a strict < so a tie goes to the first listed, which equals testing each position against the delimiters in written order; the matched occurrence is consumed whole and UnstringSkipRun repeats only the matched ALL delimiter. No edition input on the path.

refuter.evidence: Reading tested: GR12's 'Each delimiter is applied to the sending field in the sequence specified' could be read delimiter-major (scan the whole field with the first delimiter, then the next). §1985:VI.6.27.4 GR13b fixes it as position-major: 'the examination proceeds left to right until either a delimiter ... is encountered'. So the earliest position wins and the order written breaks a tie at one position, which is what UnstringExtract does (strict <). Probes (run_case.py, --std 85), u1-001: 1: 'B' OR 'AB' on 'XAB': 'AB' at position 2 wins over the first-listed 'B' at position 3 (X|AB). 6: '-' OR '-+' on 'A-+B': '-' listed first wins at position 2, then '+B', and receiver C is not acted upon (keeps ZZZZ, GR13g). 5: 'X' OR ALL ';' on 'AB;;;CD;E': AB|;|02, CD, POINTER 09. 7: 'AB' OR ALL 'A' on 'AAAB'. Each character serves in one delimiter. cite: OK  §1985:VI.6.27.4 GR12  (║6.27.4 General Rules║)  the text is in GR12; OK  §1985:VI.6.27.4 GR13b  (║6.27.4 General Rules║)  the text is in GR13b
